To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cell surface molecule recognized in sheep red blood cell rosette formation by the erythro- cyte receptor (E receptor) of T lymphocytes is a minor glycoprote- in on the sheep red cell that is also recognized by the human E receptor.

a monoclonal anti-T11TS antibody was produced that blocks E rosette-forming activity and competes with anti-T11 antibody for the E receptor; that sheep T11TS is crossreactive with human T11; and that sheep T11 is crossreactive over species with human T11TS.

we have identified the cell surface molecule recognized (and bound) by the E receptor of T lymphocyte using a monoclonallly derived mAb to sheep red blood cell (SRBC), that we have partially characterized the molecule using surface-labeled SRBc, that the molecule is a minor glycoproten of about 42,000 molecular weight, and that the molecule appears to be recognized and bound by the E receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of a new cell surface molecule, T11TS, which is recognized by the E rosette receptor.
the isolation of a molecule (T11TS) recognized by the E rosette receptor and its characterization in order to determine whether the molecule has a role in the regulation of T cell function.
a novel surface molecule, T11TS, which appears to be involved in the interaction of the E receptor with T cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T11TS is a molecule which, like the E receptor, is involved in T cell function.
the T11TS is a molecule that can bind to the T11 molecule on T cells and to sheep red cells, but not to human red cells.
the E rosetting molecule is not the T3 antigen but a different molecule which may be a member of a T cell receptor family.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
T11TS is a cell surface protein that functions in the binding of SRB cells to the T11 molecule, which is the E rosette receptor.
T11 is the E receptor and T11TS is a complementary receptor.
we have demonstrated that the sheep T cell E rosette receptor (T11) and its sheep ligand (T11TS) have a counterpart on sheep and human T lymphocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the sheep erythrocyte (SRBC) rosette receptor is a glycoprotein of 42,000 daltons that is present in both human and sheep cells, but that it is not a component of the major histocompatibility complex.
we identified a new cell surface marker that is recognized by the E rosette receptor and is involved in the activation of T cells.
T11TS is a glycoprotein that can be purified from sheep red cells and that is recognized by both the human E receptor and the T11 mAb.
